title: Align legal / design / engineering decision threads for incremental PRD slices
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: The Structured Output PRD (v2) was expanded during scoping to include three incremental slices: 1) schema validation and error surface, 2) console renderers (compact/expanded), 3) API backward-compatibility behavior (legacy clients). Each slice has distinct dependencies: legal for data classification and retention wording, design for UX patterns and accessibility, and engineering for API contract and rollout strategy. Problem: stakeholders have reviewed the PRD in separate threads causing contradictory acceptance criteria and unclear rollback gates. Goal: produce an aligned signoff plan and decision log for each incremental slice so PRD can move to Development and be included in the next release train.
acceptance_criteria: A single signed PRD acceptance artifact exists for each slice with explicit signatories from Eng, Design, Legal, and Security
Clear cutoff criteria for behavioral differences (e.g., default schema enforcement ON/OFF) documented and agreed
Rollout strategy defined: canary criteria, fallback model variant mapping, and monitoring dashboards listed
Legal checklist completed for any telemetry or example data stored; wording approved for docs and onboarding
Design handoff includes component specs, accessibility checklist, and final screenshots for console compact/expanded renderers
Engineering provides API compatibility matrix and automated contract tests included in CI
A minimal labeled rollback playbook exists for each slice with owners and SLAs for incident response
risks: Legal redlines could require removal of telemetry used by QA which would impact regression coverage
Design rework late in cycle may push the compact renderer to EOW beyond planned release
Engineering estimate variance for API compatibility layer integration could exceed sprint capacity
mitigation_plan: Hold a three-way working session (Legal + Design + Eng) to lock decisions per slice and publish a 1-page decision memo
Split signoff into tech-safe minimal viable defaults per slice to allow parallel work (e.g., default: permissive schema validation with opt-in strict mode)
Create a small canary cohort and predefine rollback criteria and owner contact list to shorten mean time to recover
